newsitem.title: PERU: Malaysian minister leaves Peru, envoy still hostage.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian minister leaves Peru, envoy still hostage.

text.p: Malaysian Foreign Minister Abdullah Ahmad Badawi left Peru on Saturday after three days of talks with government officials, apparently no closer to securing the release of his country's ambassador held by Marxist rebels.

Badawi, who came to Peru on a "special mission" for the "safe and early release" of Ahmad Mokhtar, told reporters before leaving Lima's international airport that he was pleased the ambassador was in "good condition."

The Malaysian minister's arrival in Peru had sparked speculation Kuala Lumpur was trying to cut a private deal with the rebels to free Mokhtar, held in the Japanese ambassador's residence with 102 other VIP hostages.
But the Bernama news agency reported in Malaysia that after meeting with President Alberto Fujimori, Badawi was content to leave the handling of the crisis to the Peruvian leader.
"He (Fujimori) can control the situation," Badawi was quoted as saying.
